comments.author: jedel
comments.content:
## FFE ##

[ Rationale ]

* Introduce `lustre` as a new source package in stonking/universe
  (2.17.58+dfsg-0ubuntu1): the Lustre parallel filesystem, including
  client and server userspace, and a DKMS kernel module
  package using ZFS OSD as its backend.
* Charmed Lustre is the main driver (https://charmhub.io/lustre-server). The
  charm currently uses a PPA (https://launchpad.net/~ubuntu-hpc/+archive/ubuntu/lustre-2.17)
  to install the required Lustre packages. This does not work for a formal product,
  since it doesn't give any security patches and maintenance guarantees. Landing
  in Universe formalizes the offering and ends the PPA dependency.

[ Scope ]

* New source package for the current series only.
  - Binaries: lustre-client-utils, lustre-server-utils,
    lustre-resource-agents, liblustreapi1, liblnetconfig4,
    liblustreapi-dev, liblnetconfig-dev, lustre-dkms
  - Target: stonking/universe. Goes through NEW.
* Upstream: Lustre 2.17.58
  (https://github.com/Lustre/lustre-release/tree/2.17.58). There is no
  current archive version to diff the upstream changelog against; the
  name last shipped as 1.8.5+dfsg-3.1ubuntu2 in 2013,
  and the PPA publication page already carries Launchpad's diff
  against that version. Upstream references:
  - ChangeLog at the release tag:
    https://github.com/Lustre/lustre-release/blob/2.17.58/lustre/ChangeLog
  - Changes in this point release (2.17.57..2.17.58):
    https://github.com/Lustre/lustre-release/compare/2.17.57...2.17.58
  - Supported kernels: https://wiki.whamcloud.com/display/PUB/Lustre+Support+Matrix
* `seeded-in-ubuntu lustre` output:
    The source package 'lustre' does not exist in the Ubuntu primary
    archive in stonking for pockets Release, Security, Updates,
    Proposed with status in Pending, Published
  The package is not seeded anywhere and nothing depends on it.
* No removals, no transitions, and no shared library conflicts (new
  SONAMEs: liblustreapi1, liblnetconfig4).

[ Testing ]

* Smoke test:
  - PPA: https://launchpad.net/~ubuntu-hpc/+archive/ubuntu/lustre-2.17
    (latest published upload for stonking:
    2.17.58+dfsg-0ubuntu1~ppa1~stonking10,
    https://launchpad.net/~ubuntu-hpc/+archive/ubuntu/lustre-2.17/+sourcepub/18752566/+listing-archive-extra)
  - Build: Launchpad build logs for the stonking10 upload:
    - amd64: https://launchpad.net/~ubuntu-hpc/+archive/ubuntu/lustre-2.17/+build/33622835
    - arm64: https://launchpad.net/~ubuntu-hpc/+archive/ubuntu/lustre-2.17/+build/33622837
  - Installation: fresh stonking LXD VMs. Verified with a
    three-node cluster (MDS/OSS/client) that does a remote IO read/write.
    Successful run: <link/attach>
  - Upgrade: 2.17.58+dfsg-0ubuntu1 sorts above the PPA versions
    (2.17.58+dfsg-0ubuntu1~ppa1~stonkingN), so archive installs upgrade
    over the PPA.
  - Autopkgtest: `dkms-autopkgtest` PASS. It builds and installs the
    lustre-dkms module for the running kernel inside a qemu testbed. The
    test ships in the package and will run in Ubuntu CI on publication, including
    per-kernel triggers through the dkms hook.
    Successful run: <link/attach>
  - Does it break other packages: N/A. New package, no reverse
    dependencies.

[ Regression Potential ]

* This is a new package. There are no archive users to regress and
  nothing depends on it. Potential regressions:
  - DKMS builds fail on user kernels as ABIs move. The
    autopkgtest exercises this exact build path.
  - ZFS version mismatch. The Lustre DKMS package has a dependency on
    the ZFS DKMS package for its compilation process. If the ZFS version
    used in the lustre build and the runtime ZFS mismatch, module load
    fails with "disagrees about version of symbol"; the versioned 
    zfs-dkms (>= 2.0.7) dependency prevents this by making lustre build
    against the zfs it will load.

[ Other Info ]

* Historical note: a `lustre` source package existed in Ubuntu
  universe (section admin, 1.8.5+dfsg-3.1ubuntu2) until it was removed
  during the Trusty cycle (RoQA, Debian #690459, "does not work with
  Debian Linux kernel packages"). This upload is an entirely new
  packaging of upstream 2.17.58; the old binaries only ever shipped to
  series that are EOL today, so there is no upgrade path to consider.
* This bug is also the heads-up for the Kernel team and Archive Admins:
  production deployments with secure boot need signed kernel modules,
  and the plan is for the Kernel team to build and sign kernel-flavor
  Lustre module packages once the userspace and DKMS package is in the
  archive.

comments.author: athos
comments.content:
Thanks, José.

I reviewed your stonking branch in github and the package LGTM.

I intend to upload this once we get an AA pre-approval, as described in https://ubuntu.com/project/docs/release-team/freezes/#new-packages.

comments.author: paelzer
comments.content:
Thank you,
I'm somewhat aware of the reasoning and case itself, let me have a look at the outcome of this cooperation ...


Thanks for the extra confidence of not being a late rushed crap due to providing install logs, test logs and generally outlining the details and what you did. It shows that you really thought about impact, regressions and more.

I checked the upload in the PPA as if it would be in NEW queue, namespacing (lustes- and lib names that match) and licenses (no warnings) are fine.
The packaging best practises you already iterated on the last few days.

Thanks!

Ask in regard to the changelog (maybe it is in git but not in the PPA uploads I checked):
- it is almost a hard requirement to map to this bug there, please add "(LP: #2168274)"
- it would be lovely but not required if there could be a bit of a summary what was done (not all details, but high level if you started from scratch and why some options have been chosen, ...) This is almost free text and a bit more than "Initial release" would help. I know that you know what it is all about, but others do not.

AA pre-ack for this case under https://ubuntu.com/project/docs/release-team/freezes/#new-packages
